newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases on sufficient liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases on sufficient liquidity.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down to 12.0/13.0 percent from 14.0/15.0 percent on Wednesday on the back of sufficient liquidity supply in the market, dealers said.
One foreign bank dealer said there was some carry-forward impact from Tuesday's close at the opening which kept the overnight rate trading at around 14.5 percent.
"But it eased down gradually as operators gained confidence that the condition had stabilised," he said.
Operators were cautious on Tuesday about a possible repeat of the extremely tight liquidity condition last Friday.
Dealers said longer-term rates were seen easing slightly, with one-week and one-month money trading at around 13.75/14.00 and 14.125/14.375 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 14.01 percent against 12.20 percent on Monday.
